extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting to F1000 publishing venues; researchers interested in becoming peer reviewers; current reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines describing F1000's fully open, post-publication peer review process: how it operates, reviewer requirements, status labels, and instructions for authors and reviewers on participation and revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open peer review is the term used to describe any peer review model where aspects of research evaluation are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some of the most common hallmarks of open peer review include open identities, open peer review reports, and open participation from the research community.

rubrics_metrics.name: F1000 post-publication open peer review model
rubrics_metrics.description: All F1000 publishing venues operate a post-publication open peer review model: accepted articles are published before peer review takes place so research can be viewed and cited immediately while signaling that the article is awaiting review by experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review reports are published alongside the article for anyone to read; reviewer names and affiliations are published with the peer review report; any registered users can comment on the article to engage in discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review status: Awaiting peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles are labeled with the status 'Awaiting peer review' immediately upon publication to signal to readers that the research is yet to be reviewed by expert reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As soon as a peer review report is published, the peer review status is updated to reflect the article’s new approval status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review status: Approved
rubrics_metrics.description: No, or only minor changes are required. For original research, this means that the aims and research methods are adequate; results are presented accurately, and the conclusions are justified and supported by the presented data or supporting material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may suggest small changes to improve the article or correct minor errors, but these changes will not affect the peer review status. A peer review report accompanied by a green tick indicates that the article has been 'Approved'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review status: Approved with reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer believes the article has academic merit but has asked for several small changes to the article or specific, sometimes more significant, revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should have made clear that the changes requested are necessary for an 'Approved' status to be awarded. A peer review report accompanied by a green question mark indicates that the article has been 'Approved with reservations'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review status: Not approved
rubrics_metrics.description: The article in its current form has issues that seriously undermine the findings and conclusions. Crucial substantial revisions will be required for the paper to pass peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Not approved' is not a rejection — it is possible to improve an article’s status from 'Not approved' to 'Approved' upon publication of a new version. A peer review report accompanied by a red cross indicates that the article is 'Not approved'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author requirement: suggest five potential reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted authors are asked to suggest five potential reviewers for their article; authors must provide at least five reviewer suggestions that meet the reviewer criteria before an article can be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After publication, authors are expected to continue suggesting reviewers until at least two reviews have been received. The Editorial team will work with authors to ensure chosen reviewers meet the criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer criterion: Qualified
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should typically hold a doctorate (Ph.D./MD/MBBS or equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions will be made for scholarly disciplines where doctorates are not necessary. When applying to be a reviewer, contact the Editorial office and attach a CV and complete the reviewer form so the team can confirm you meet the Reviewer Criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer criterion: Impartial (no competing interests)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not have any competing interests that can bias their assessment of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They should not be close collaborators of authors or be personally associated with them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer criterion: Expert (publication record)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should have published at least three articles as lead author in a relevant topic, with at least one article having been published in the last five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer criterion: Institutional and geographic diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: We require that reviewers are from different institutions and strongly encourage authors to suggest geographically-diverse reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geographic diversity is encouraged to gain an international perspective on the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to reviewers and revised versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to respond to reviewers after receiving two peer review reports; revising the article should address questions or minor errors identified in reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors who submit a revised article version should provide a direct point-by-point response to each reviewer explaining how each comment has been addressed. Reviewers may then update the peer review status. All versions of the article, and all peer review reports, remain published so the article history is visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of peer review reports and reviewer identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review reports are published alongside the article and reviewer names and affiliations are published with the peer review report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This transparency allows anyone to read reports and enables open discussion via registered-user comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals and benefits of open peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000 uses open peer review to: start open and transparent conversations; allow research to be cited immediately; reduce the possibility of bias; empower authors to lead the process; enable open, constructive feedback; improve the quality of peer review; and increase opportunities for collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becoming a peer reviewer (process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers wishing to be reviewers should contact the Editorial office, attach a copy of their CV and complete the reviewer form so the Editorial team can confirm they meet the Reviewer Criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may indicate particular articles you'd like to be considered for, but it is up to the authors whether they would like you to review their article.
